\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آنسو} (ā̃sū)}{آنسو (ā̃sū)}]{\ur{آنسو} (ā̃sū) — tears}

\label{lesson:UR-C257-asu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a host, then the Urdu for people.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آنسو}}
\textbf{\ur{آنسو}} — \emph{ā̃sū} — \textquotedblleft{}tears\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آنسو}} (\emph{ā̃sū}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{aśru}, \textquotedblleft{}tear\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 919). CDIAL notes that the word took a nasal vowel early, as the word for \textquotedblleft{}eye\textquotedblright{} did.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā̃sū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ā̃sū}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a host, then the Urdu for people, then say \emph{ā̃sū} again
\end{itemize}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for people, then the Urdu for tears.

\textbf{\ur{مسکراہٹ}} — \emph{muskurāhaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a smile\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{محبت} (mohabbat)}{محبت (mohabbat)}]{\ur{محبت} (mohabbat) — affection, love}

\label{lesson:UR-C257-mohabbat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for tears, then the Urdu for a smile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{محبت}}
\textbf{\ur{محبت}} — \emph{mohabbat} — \textquotedblleft{}affection, love\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{محبت}} (\emph{mohabbat}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{maḥabba}, \textquotedblleft{}love, affection\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{ḥ-b-b} (Lane). It is built on the same root as \emph{ḥubb}, \textquotedblleft{}love\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
